nodes.label: memory transport
nodes.rationale: For tests and examples.

nodes.label: Keep a Changelog and semantic versioning
nodes.rationale: Versions track @fyrlabs/dead-drop; transport-sdk versions independently and its changes are called out explicitly.

nodes.label: expose prints the peer's connect command (0.12.0)
nodes.rationale: Finding your own peer id used to be a separate command you had to know about; a directory now names the exposure after itself, while --target still needs --name because a url has no obvious name in it.

nodes.label: polling and policy validated at config load (0.12.0)
nodes.rationale: An unknown key, a number written as a string, a policy.primary that is not a name or a polling minimum above its maximum used to be accepted and then quietly do nothing; each now stops start-up with the field named.

nodes.label: parallel policy actually fans out (0.11.0)
nodes.rationale: It used to be accepted and then quietly ignored, picking one transport like the default mode, so nobody who set it ever got a second copy.

nodes.label: inboxOrphanMs orphan mail reaping (0.10.0)
nodes.rationale: Only the addressed peer empties its inbox, so mail for a peer that never returns was unreclaimable storage (one trial repo squashed to a single commit still held 60 MB). Any peer now deletes such a message once it is older than 7 days AND its recipient has stopped publishing a presence beacon, so a peer merely offline for days keeps its mail.

nodes.label: compactAfterCommits data-branch compaction (0.8.0)
nodes.rationale: Every message left a commit behind for good, so joining a long-lived workspace kept getting slower. Past 500 commits whichever peer notices first replaces the branch with a single commit; turn it off where the branch is protected against force-pushes, and note compaction discards the commit log.

nodes.label: ddrop dashboard on 127.0.0.1:7373 (0.7.0)
nodes.rationale: Read-only, starts no runtime, reads the same control socket ddrop status does, and ships its page inside the package so it renders with no network. Anything with local access can read workspace metadata from the port, so run it while looking at it rather than as a service.

nodes.label: ddrop queues reads object keys only (0.6.0)
nodes.rationale: Nothing is decrypted and nothing is consumed, so you can see a peer that has stopped keeping up without waiting for a request to time out.

nodes.label: discover distinguishes unreachable from empty (0.6.0)
nodes.rationale: It used to say 'No peers have announced themselves yet' and exit 0 when it could not reach any transport, so an unreachable workspace looked like an empty one.

nodes.label: transport-sdk 1.1.0 nested prefix listing check
nodes.rationale: A third-party adapter that listed only direct children would have reported every queue as empty.

nodes.label: workspace concurrency setting (0.5.0)
nodes.rationale: Default 1; raising it removes head-of-line blocking behind a slow handler at the cost of answering messages out of send order.

nodes.label: healthIntervalMs (0.5.0)
nodes.rationale: Default 30000; lower where probing is cheap, raise for github where every sweep spends an API call.

nodes.label: presenceIntervalMs (0.5.0)
nodes.rationale: Default 30000 leaves discovery up to 90 seconds stale; lower on a shared folder, leave alone on git where every beacon is a commit.

nodes.label: retry and breaker configurable (0.4.1)
nodes.rationale: Raising retry.maxAttempts alone usually buys nothing because since 0.3.0 the request timeout bounds the whole request, so extra attempts are cut off by the deadline; raise requestTimeoutMs with it.

nodes.label: init writes a config that works (0.4.0)
nodes.rationale: It generates the secret into .deaddrop/secret, writes the peer id explicitly so two peers no longer default to the same hostname and collide, and marks the shared location REPLACE-ME instead of quietly defaulting to a local folder that two people could never share.

nodes.label: ${file:PATH} and ${env:NAME} config interpolation (0.4.0)
nodes.rationale: Relative paths resolve against the config file and whitespace is stripped, so a config can be committed with the secret beside it rather than inside it.

nodes.label: REPLACE-ME placeholder fails at start-up (0.4.0)
Correction of the 'never in clear text' claim (0.2.3, 0.4.0)
nodes.rationale: The 0.1.0 notes and the README claimed channel, peer and workspace names never appear in clear text while listing object keys as unprotected two paragraphs later; keys carry those names deliberately, so the claim was corrected along with AGENTS.md invariant 9.

nodes.label: git transport no longer takes over an enclosing repository (0.3.1)
nodes.rationale: The quick start invited a relative workDir inside one of your own checkouts, and the transport then repointed origin, rewrote the commit name and email, and checked out its data branch over your work.

nodes.label: Runtime starts even when no transport is reachable (0.3.1)
nodes.rationale: ddrop connect used to wait for the first presence beacon before binding its local port, so during an outage callers saw connection refused with nothing in the log.

nodes.label: Presence beacons no longer pile up on a slow transport (0.3.1)
nodes.rationale: Only one is published at a time and it is abandoned once too old to be believed, so a merely slow backend is not pushed into failing by its own presence records.

nodes.label: A transport that failed to start once can recover (0.3.1)
nodes.rationale: The git and GitHub transports cached the first clone or auth failure and re-threw it for the life of the process, so a momentary network fault left a transport that could never recover whatever its breaker did.

nodes.label: Request timeout bounds the whole request (0.3.0)
nodes.rationale: It used to guard only the wait for a reply, so a caller asking for 15 seconds could wait two minutes while transports failed; a transport legitimately slower than the deadline now fails at it instead of succeeding late.

nodes.label: Failover no longer backs off in front of an open breaker (0.3.0)
nodes.rationale: The manager moves to the next transport immediately, which is why the fallback was configured; failover takes seconds instead of minutes.

nodes.label: allowPeers matches the caller's configured peerId (0.3.0)
nodes.rationale: It used to match the reply address, a per-process value for a ddrop connect client that appears in no config file, so a hand-written list matched nobody and denied everyone.

nodes.label: Peer id split into mailbox address and identity (0.3.0)
nodes.rationale: One id was doing two jobs; separating them lets a short-lived session take its own address without losing who it is.

nodes.label: Timeout during an in-flight send no longer crashes the runtime (0.2.6)
Missing exposure returns NOT_FOUND 404 instead of DECODE_FAILED 500 (0.2.6)
Two-tier e2e suite: fast and live (0.2.6)
nodes.rationale: Every scenario states what a user can and cannot do; it first covered broadcast, key rotation, transport failover, message expiry, allowPeers and the http exposure type, and writing it produced two of the release's fixes.

nodes.label: Second runtime clones into <workDir>.peers/ (0.2.5)
nodes.rationale: Two runtimes cannot share one git working tree, which git does not support; the first to start claims the directory, abandoned clones are removed at next start, and this mainly affects ddrop connect, which builds its runtime from the same config file.

nodes.label: A push counts as published only once the commit is on the remote-tracking branch (0.2.4)
nodes.rationale: git push exits 0 saying 'Everything up-to-date' when its commit is no longer HEAD, which happens whenever a second process shares the clone; a live GitHub run lost 10 of 50 requests to this.

nodes.label: Non-retryable health failures logged at error level (0.2.3)
nodes.rationale: A wrong repo let the runtime report 'runtime started' and flap its breaker forever while the transport's own actionable message reached no log at any level.

nodes.label: Version read from the package manifest (0.2.1, 0.2.2)
nodes.rationale: A hard-coded literal reported 0.1.0 from a 0.2.0 install and fed the runtime, so ddrop status and /health reported it too; a test now fails the build if any source file hard-codes one.

nodes.label: Hashed short socket path under temp (0.2.1)
nodes.rationale: A Unix socket path cannot exceed 104 bytes and init writes a relative .deaddrop resolved against the working directory, so any project deeper than about 84 characters hit listen EINVAL. Runtime and client commands derive the fallback the same way, so discovery is unaffected.

nodes.label: Consolidation from ten packages to two (0.2.0, breaking)
nodes.rationale: Everything except the transport contract lives in @fyrlabs/dead-drop reachable by subpath; transport-sdk stays separate so a third-party adapter does not depend on the whole runtime.

nodes.label: Error model moved into transport-sdk (0.2.0, breaking)
nodes.rationale: A transport adapter has to throw DeadDropError and the transport manager reads its retryable flag, so the error model belongs in the contract; the protocol layer re-exports it for compatibility.

nodes.label: DeadDropError.is brand-checks Symbol.for (0.2.0)
nodes.rationale: Previously an error crossing two copies of transport-sdk was re-wrapped as INTERNAL, which is retryable, so a permanent failure like UNAUTHORIZED would be retried indefinitely.

nodes.label: Built-in transports load through static import() thunks (0.2.0)
nodes.rationale: A dynamic import(variable) cannot be resolved relative to the importing module by bundlers or test runners, so the previous specifier-string form worked under plain Node and failed everywhere else.

nodes.label: Release workflow skips an already-published package (0.2.0)
nodes.rationale: It used to abort the whole job before the package that did change got published.

nodes.label: eslint no-restricted-imports replaced package-boundary layering (0.2.0)
nodes.rationale: Same direction inside one package: protocol imports nothing above it, core never names a transport, and a transport sees only the protocol and the transport SDK.

nodes.label: At-least-once delivery machinery over plain object storage (0.1.0)
nodes.rationale: Framing, chunking, delete-as-acknowledgement, redelivery with backoff, dead letters, deduplication, retained broadcast topics, and polling that adapts to traffic.

nodes.label: Proxy mode (0.1.0)
nodes.rationale: expose --target makes an unmodified local server reachable to peers and connect serves it back as an ordinary local URL; static directory exposures too.

nodes.label: Observability: JSON logs with redaction, Prometheus metrics, tracing (0.1.0)
nodes.rationale: A message id is its own trace id, so ddrop trace <requestId> works with the id a timeout error already returns.

nodes.label: Multiple transports with health scoring, jittered retry, breaking and failover (0.1.0)
Plugin contract and framework-agnostic conformance suite (0.1.0)
nodes.rationale: A store adapter is four methods.

nodes.label: Responses buffered whole and capped at 32 MiB
nodes.rationale: Streaming is not implemented.

nodes.label: Duplicates are suppressed, not prevented
nodes.rationale: Ordering is best-effort per recipient, so handlers must be safe to run twice.

hyperedges.label: Transport resilience flow: health scoring, retry, breaker, failover and honest retryable errors
